precepts.text: The Levites were given to Aaron to do the service of the tabernacle and were set apart to this office.
precepts.point: He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel: that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary.” The Levites were given to Aaron to do the service of the tabernacle, set apart to this office.

That is why David declared, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath the Lord chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.” He prepared a place for the ark in the city of David and pitched a tent for it, and this time he set it in the hands of those the Most High had chosen.

precepts.text: Uzza handled the ark when he was not to and died for it, showing why this order matters.
precepts.point: He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” Uzza handled the ark when he was not to, and he died for it.

That shows why this order matters. David had seen what happens when the ark is not carried the way the Most High commanded, so now he says, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites”.

precepts.text: The staves are set in the rings so the ark is borne, and the staves are not to be taken out.
precepts.point: The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, that the ark may be borne with them. The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.” The staves are set in the rings so the ark is borne, and they are not to be taken out.

The first attempt failed, “for that we sought him not after the due order.” This time “the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord.” The due order is the order Moses was given.

precepts.text: The priests could not deal with holy things while unclean, so they had to be clean before serving.
precepts.point: The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.” The priests could not deal with holy things while unclean, so they had to be clean before serving.

That is why David charged the chief of the fathers of the Levites, “sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel unto the place that I have prepared for it.” “So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel.”

precepts.text: David and the elders of Israel went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obededom with joy.
precepts.point: The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.
precepts.why:
“So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obed–edom with joy.”

That is the other account of the ark coming up to Jerusalem, the place David had prepared for it. Line up Second Samuel 6 and First Chronicles 15 and you have the history of how the ark came to be in Jerusalem before Solomon was strengthened in his kingdom.
